title: UPS Runtime Reduction: Battery Technology Trade-offs for Short-Duration Backup
snippet: Tod Higinbotham, COO of ZincFive, explores the race to reduce uninterruptible power supply (UPS) runtimes.
description: ZincFive COO examines shift from 30-minute to 3-minute UPS runtimes and battery technology constraints around power density, discharge rates, and oversizing.
so_what: Runtime compression to 3 minutes forces battery selection around power density vs discharge rate tradeoffs, driving oversizing costs and floor space loss.
summary: Article explores data center shift from 30-minute to sub-5-minute (now targeting 3-minute) UPS runtimes enabled by faster generator failover. Lead-acid lacks power density for short bursts; lithium-ion BMS shutdowns prevent high discharge rates; both require costly oversizing to compensate for cell failure modes.
why_it_matters: Facilities operators designing UPS systems face direct trade-offs between battery chemistry, cabinet footprint, and failover reliability. Lead-acid requires more cabinets due to low energy density; lithium-ion BMS auto-shutdowns during high discharge can cripple UPS during outages. Single-cell failures in either technology create open circuits that kill entire strings, forcing oversizing decisions that consume revenue-generating floor space.
